Hi Samir (and team),

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and a short list of follow-ups we promised to capture so we can scope the dedicated/reserved capacity recommendation and the SDK/auth integration work:

What we covered (brief):
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + reranking for search results; embeddings used for retrieval; tool-calls used for ticket lookups (~10% of requests).
- Preference for a private/reserved pool (data controls + consistent latency).

Clarifying questions we need to finalize sizing and integration plan:
1) Traffic profile
   - Peak QPS (concurrent inference requests) vs steady QPS — you mentioned a spike pattern around business hours; can you confirm expected peak concurrent requests and % of calls that are multi-turn/chat vs single-shot?
2) Payload and context
   - Median and 95th percentile context length (tokens) for generation and how often the reranker needs full-document embeddings.
3) Auth & provisioning
   - Do you prefer SAML-based SSO for user sessions and OAuth2 client credentials for service-to-service (recommended)? Any enterprise constraints (IP allowlists, proxy)?
4) SDKs and languages
   - Which languages will you bootstrap first (Python/Node/Java)? We’ll prepare example bootstraps and an auth flow for the selected SDKs.
5) Routing & fallbacks
   - Priority: low-latency vs low-cost during congestion? Also whether you want sticky routing per-customer or round-robin.
6) Reranker/Embeddings throughput
   - Expected qps for embedding generation and reranker throughput (if you have per-minute numbers that helps).

Attachments: I’ve attached a preliminary capacity proposal and an SDK/auth checklist — these are placeholders so we can iterate after you confirm traffic numbers.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Samir: confirm the numbers above (peak QPS, token-length percentiles, % tool-calls) — earliest by EOD tomorrow if possible.
- Ben/Camila (internal): prepare a 30–45 minute technical deep-dive that covers SDK auth flows, routing policies, and an autoscale/queue model.
- We’ll follow with a capacity recommendation for a reserved pool (min/burst sizing + concurrency limits) and a short playbook for integration.

Thanks — Marcus

Thanks Marcus — great write-up. Quick answers below so you can start sizing:

Traffic and profile:
- Baseline steady QPS: ~55 qps (single-shot ranking + small generation).
- Peak concurrent QPS: plan for spikes up to 160 qps during promo windows (~11:30–13:30 PST).
- About 18% of calls are multi-turn (chat sessions that keep context).

Payload/context:
- Median context ~700 tokens; 95th ~3,200 tokens (longest are multi-doc summaries).
- Reranker uses embeddings of ~512 dims; we do batches of 8–16 items for rerank.

Auth/provisioning:
- We require SAML SSO for user access; for service-to-service we’ll use OAuth2 client credentials + our internal secrets manager. IP allowlist possible but prefer mutual TLS.

SDKs:
- Start with Python and Node; Java second wave.

Routing/fallbacks:
- Preference: prioritize latency (we want stable 95th pct tail), but we’ll accept cost-based fallbacks that preserve availability (route to cheaper variant when non-critical). Sticky routing per customer would be useful for session affinities.

Reranker/embeddings throughput:
- Embedding requests: ~3,200/min at peak (roughly 53/min average). Reranker throughput: roughly 1,800 rerank operations/minute at peak.

Availability for deep-dive:
- We can do Wednesday 8 Dec 09:00–09:45 PT. Anita (cc’d) will own security/compliance questions.

Folks — adding a few technical notes based on Samir’s numbers that will inform the reserved capacity recommendation:

Autoscale / reserved pool proposal (initial):
- Min pool: 4 GPU workers (for baseline 55 qps).
- Baseline worker concurrency: target 6 concurrent requests per worker for generation-heavy workloads; for reranker/embeddings we plan separate worker types or model variants to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Burst: autoscale up to 16 workers during peak traffic (160 qps) with a fast ramp policy (30s increments) and queue backpressure when >200 requests queued.

Concurrency and queues:
- Per-worker soft concurrency limit: 6–8 (depends on per-request latency and memory).
- Global request queue per-pool with priority lanes: interactive (latency-sensitive) vs batch (rerank/embeddings). Interactive lane preempts batch up to a limit.

Routing / stickiness:
- Support for sticky routing by customer id (hashing) to preserve KV cache locality. This helps keep prompt prefix caches warm and reduces tokens served.

Model variants and fallbacks:
- Primary generation: full-precision RLHF model.
- Cost fallback: quantized candidate that preserves output quality for non-critical traffic.

Embeddings/rerankers:
- Separate embedding workers with higher throughput (batch size 64–128) — recommend provisioning a dedicated embedding pool; we can autoscale based on queue depth.
- Reranker: recommend 8-bit quantized reranker model for throughput, run in an instance type optimized for short-latency inferencing.

Telemetry and SLAs:
- Need access to sample payloads and error/timeout tolerances to size tail latency SLOs (95th target: sub-350ms for interactive tokens).

I’ll attach a quick capacity/queue model csv and a draft autoscale policy you can review. Camila — can you prepare the short slide for the Wed deep-dive showing routing lanes and queue behavior?

-ben
